questions.q: Researchers have long believed that memories form due to changes in the brain ___
questions.explanation: Memories are thought to be stored through changes in neurons, especially in the strength of synaptic connections between them (e.g., long-term potentiation). Muscles, bones and blood are not where memories are formed.

questions.q: ___ refers to calling back the stored information in response to some cue for use in a process or activity
questions.explanation: Retrieval is the process of accessing stored information in response to a cue so it can be used. Encoding converts information into a storable form, and storage keeps it over time.

questions.q: The duration of the sensory register is ___
questions.explanation: The sensory register holds a large amount of raw sensory information only very briefly, roughly up to 1-3 seconds (visual traces fade in under a second, auditory ones last a little longer). 15-30 seconds is the typical duration of unrehearsed short-term memory.

questions.q: Maintenance rehearsal in the context of short term memory is also known as ___
questions.explanation: Maintenance rehearsal, simply repeating information to keep it in short-term memory, is also called rote rehearsal. Elaborative rehearsal is different, as it links the information to meaning and existing knowledge.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a component of the working memory model?
questions.explanation: Baddeley's working memory model has a central executive, phonological loop, visuo-spatial sketchpad and episodic buffer. There is no 'language repository' component; verbal material is handled by the phonological loop.

questions.q: ___ describes our implicit knowledge of tasks that usually do not require conscious recall to perform them
questions.explanation: Procedural memory is implicit memory for skills and how to do things, such as riding a bicycle, performed without conscious recall. Declarative memory (semantic and episodic) is explicit memory for facts and events.

questions.q: The Levels of Processing theory in memory is given by -
questions.explanation: Fergus Craik and Robert Lockhart proposed the levels of processing theory in 1972, arguing that deeper (semantic) processing produces more durable memories. Atkinson and Shiffrin proposed the multi-store model, and Baddeley the working memory model.

questions.q: ___ processing is when we encode only the physical qualities of something.
questions.explanation: Structural (shallow) processing encodes only physical features, such as what a word looks like. Phonemic processing encodes sound, and semantic processing encodes meaning, which is the deepest level.

questions.q: ___ refers to the cognitive capacity actually allocated to the task.
questions.explanation: In cognitive load theory, mental effort is the cognitive capacity actually allocated to a task. Mental load is the load imposed by the task itself, and performance is the outcome achieved.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a helpful way of improving memory?
questions.explanation: Writing things down, repetition, visual imagery and attaching meaning are all well-supported memory aids. Over-exerting yourself causes fatigue and stress, which impair rather than improve memory.
